key_insight: A finite-temperature quantum quasinormal-mode theory describes lossy, non-reciprocal cavity magnonic systems while accounting for material dissipation, radiation losses, and thermal fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports quantitative design of hybrid photon–magnon–qubit devices under realistic open-system and thermal conditions.
method: Combine macroscopic quantum electrodynamics for non-reciprocal media with complex coordinate transformations.
Quantize quasinormal modes in spatially inhomogeneous, dissipative, dispersive resonators.
Apply the theory to hybrid dielectric–magnonic resonators coupled to spin and superconducting qubits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical applications showing modal interference, a coherent-to-dissipative coupling transition, spatiotemporal quantum fields, and magnon-mediated qubit synchronization at zero and finite temperatures.
watch_item: The abstract does not report experimental validation or computational scaling, leaving practical accuracy and implementation cost to be assessed.
paper_title: Finite-temperature Quantum Quasinormal Mode Theory for Spatiotemporally-resolved Dissipative Cavity Quantum Magnonics
